Variation 3: Pumpkintop Shandy. A pumpkin ale (such as Southern Tier's Pumpking Imperial) + ginger beer + a squeeze of orange juice + an orange slice.

Beer Cocktails.Recipe: Get The Right Beer With This Interactive Craft Beer Guide
Yuengling Hershey's Chocolate Porter Is Coming Back in 2020 Thanks to Demand

Direction: Pour water into a large saucepan and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and add orange spice tea bags. Cover and let steep for 5 minutes.
Remove tea bags and stir in apple cider, rum, brown sugar, and 2 cinnamon sticks. Heat cider over medium-low heat until just steaming.
Ladle hot cider into 6 mugs and drop 1/2 teaspoon butter into each. Garnish with a cinnamon "swizzle" stick.
Gather all ingredients.

Place a filter in the basket of an automatic coffee maker. Add brown sugar, cinnamon stick, cloves, allspice, salt, and nutmeg to the basket; top with orange wedges. Pour apple cider into the water reservoir.
Brew and serve hot.
Gather the ingredients.

Place apples in a large stockpot; cover with water by at least 2 inches. Stir in sugar, cinnamon, and allspice. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Boil, uncovered, for 1 hour. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Strain apple mixture through a fine-mesh sieve; discard solids. Drain cider again through a cheesecloth-lined sieve.
Serve warm or refrigerate cider until cold.
Enjoy!
Gather all ingredients.
Combine apple cider and cinnamon sticks in a slow cooker.
Place allspice and cloves onto the center of an 8-inch square piece of cheesecloth.

Gather edges of the cheesecloth together and tie to secure; place in the slow cooker. Stir in brown sugar. Cook on High, covered, until mixture is steaming and sugar has dissolved. Reduce heat to Low and keep warm.
Gather the ingredients.
Pour apple cider and maple syrup into a large stainless steel saucepan.

Place cinnamon sticks, cloves, allspice berries, orange peel, and lemon peel in the center of a square of washed cheesecloth; fold up the sides of the cheesecloth to enclose the bundle, then tie it up with a length of kitchen string. Drop the spice bundle into the cider mixture.
Place the saucepan over moderate heat and cook until cider is very hot but not boiling, about 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove cider from the heat. Discard the spice bundle.
Ladle cider into big cups or mugs, adding a fresh cinnamon stick to each serving if desired.

Cider.Recipe: Apple Pie in a Jar Drink
Ingredients: 1 ½ cups white sugar, or to taste
1 (1 liter) bottle 190 proof grain alcohol (such as Everclear)
Direction: Place apple cider, apple juice, sugar, and cinnamon sticks into a large pot. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until sugar has dissolved. Remove from heat and discard cinnamon sticks. Allow mixture to cool to room temperature, then stir in grain alcohol.
Pour into sterilized quart-sized canning jars; seal with clean lids and rings and refrigerate until ready to serve. Store in the refrigerator for up to 6 months.
Gather all ingredients.
Stir apple cider, orange juice, sugar, lemon juice, and pineapple juice together in a large pot over medium-low heat.
Place cinnamon and cloves in a tea ball and add to apple cider mixture; simmer until warmed through, about 15 minutes.
Serve from the pot with a large ladle.

Pour apple cider, pineapple juice, and cranberry juice into a stockpot. Place orange slices, cinnamon sticks, allspice berries, and cloves in a muslin pouch or directly into the apple cider mixture. Bring apple cider mixture to a boil; reduce heat and simmer until flavors have blended, 15 to 20 minutes. Remove orange slices and spices before serving.
Add prosecco and club soda to a glass. Top off with Apple Cider Syrup. Garnish with apple slices and a cinnamon stick.

Ingredients: ¼ cup brown sugar, plus 1 tablespoon divided
Direction: Combine apple cider, apple brandy, ¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon brown sugar, honey, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, pepper, and salt in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Simmer until flavors combine, about 10 minutes.
Pour apple cider mixture into heat-proof mugs. Twist orange zest strips between fingers to release essential oils; drop 1 into each mug. Add 1 cinnamon stick to each mug.

Combine apple cider, orange juice, pineapple juice, cinnamon sticks, cloves, and honey in a large stockpot over medium heat. Bring to a boil, then simmer over low heat, or transfer to a slow cooker to keep warm while serving. Strain out cinnamon sticks and cloves before serving if desired.
Combine apple cider, cranberry juice, lemon slices, brown sugar, cinnamon sticks, and cloves in a large pot; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Use a slotted spoon to remove lemon slices, cinnamon, and cloves. Serve hot.

In a large saucepan or pot, combine cider, cranberry juice, lemon juice, pineapple juice, orange slices, cloves, honey, sugar, and cinnamon sticks. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer; add nutmeg, ginger, and allspice. Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm and garnish each cup with mint and an orange slice.
For a bolder taste, refrigerate the wassail for a couple of days and reheat on the stove.

Place apples in a multi-functional pressure cooker (such as Instant Pot). Spread brown sugar, cinnamon sticks, nutmeg, and cloves on top. Fill the rest of the pot up with water, up to the maximum line. Close and lock the lid. Select high pressure according to the manufacturer’s instructions; set the timer for 60 minutes. Allow 10 to 15 minutes for pressure to build.

Release pressure carefully using the quick-release method according to the manufacturer’s instructions, about 5 minutes. Unlock and remove the lid. Remove cinnamon sticks. Mash apples with a potato masher or spoon. Return cinnamon sticks to the pot.
Continue cooking on high pressure for another 60 minutes, allowing 10 to 15 minutes for pressure to build.
Repeat quick-release, about 5 minutes. Strain out cider using a strainer or cheesecloth; discard solids.
My favorite apples to mix are Honey Crisp, Granny Smith, Pink Lady, and Gala.

Stir the apple juice, pineapple juice, and cranberry juice together with the brown sugar in a large pan. Place the cinnamon sticks, cloves, and ground allspice into a large teaball or cheesecloth bag. Place the spice bag into the pan with the juice mixture. Heat the juice mixture over medium-high heat about 10 minutes. Serve hot.

Ingredients: 3  cinnamon sticks, plus more for garnish
½ teaspoon whole cloves, or to taste
Direction: Combine apple cider, cinnamon sticks, lemon zest, cloves, nutmeg, and allspice in the inner pot of a multi-functional pressure cooker (such as Instant Pot®). Close and lock the lid. Select high pressure according to manufacturer's instructions; set timer for 1 minute. Allow 10 to 15 minutes for pressure to build.
Release pressure using the natural-release method according to manufacturer's instructions, about 15 minutes. Unlock and remove the lid.
Ladle mulled cider into cups and sweeten with honey. Garnish with lemon slices and additional cinnamon sticks.

Ingredients: 1 cup orange flavored drink mix (such as Tang®)
Direction: Combine sugar, orange flavored drink mix, tea powder, cinnamon, and cloves in a large bowl. Store in a sealed container.
To serve, mix 2 to 3 tablespoons of the mixture with a cup of hot water.
Sometimes I like to experiment with additional flavors in this mix. Other spices to consider are nutmeg, ginger, etc.

Bring cider and maple syrup just to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat. Add tea bags, ginger, and cardamom. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Remove and discard tea bags and spices. Stir in bourbon and lemon juice.
Transfer to a warmed 32- to 40-ounce thermos.
You can use pear cider instead of apple.
For a chilled cocktail, after removing tea bags and spices, put saucepan in a bowl of ice water and stir occasionally until chilled. Add bourbon and lemon juice; transfer to a chilled thermos.
The right temp! Warm a thermos by filling it with boiling water. Drain when ready to add the cocktail. For cold drinks, do the same, but fill with ice instead of hot water.

Cider.Recipe: Danny's Warm and Fuzzy Apple Cider
Direction: Combine the cider and brown sugar in a saucepan. Wrap the cinnamon sticks, allspice, cloves and lemon zest in cheesecloth and add to the cider mixture; bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes. Remove the spice bundle and stir in the rum and butterscotch schnapps. Serve warm in mugs.

Peel the skin from the orange leaving the bitter white pith behind. Stick the cloves into the skin. Squeeze the juice from the orange and add to the 2-3/4 cups orange juice. Place all ingredients into a large nonreactive pan and bring to a boil over high heat. Remove from heat, cover and allow to stand at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to blend. Serve warm or cold.

Combine orange juice, apple cider, orange slices, lime slices, cinnamon sticks, cloves, and star anise in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, about 5 minutes. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove cinnamon sticks, cloves, and star anise. Stir in honey until dissolved and keep warm.
Pour warm cider into cups. Garnish each with a cinnamon stick for stirring and several orange and lime slices.
If you're serving a large crowd, feel free to scale up the recipe, and keep warm in a slow cooker for guests to serve themselves.

Ingredients: 4 ⅛ inch piece fresh ginger, cut into thin slices
Direction: Gather the ingredients.
Tie cloves, cardamom pods, allspice berries, and star anise together in a cheesecloth sachet.
Combine apple cider, cranberry juice, and brown sugar together in a pot; bring to a simmer. Add cinnamon sticks, ginger, and spice sachet to cider mixture and steep for 20 minutes.
Pour 1 fluid ounce bourbon into each mug and top off with spiced cider.
Rub the edge of each mug with orange peel and drop into the drink.

This is perfect made in a slow cooker! You can keep adding apple cider, cranberry juice, and brown sugar to the pot as you take out for serving. It is good to squeeze the orange skin above the drink before rubbing it on the edge of the mug. This releases oils that will benefit the final product!

Cocktails.Recipe: 25 Popular Cocktail Recipes You Just Have to Know if You Love Making Drinks at Home
12 Tiki Drinks You Have to Make
25 Frozen Cocktails You'll Want to Make All Summer Long

Direction: Sprinkle celery salt onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a highball or pint glass with lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the salt. Fill the glass with ice.

Add gin, lemon juice, Tabasco sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and tomato juice to the glass. Sprinkle with a pinch of celery salt, if desired, then gently stir to combine. Garnish with lime wedge, celery stick, and any additional toppings.
For peppermint infusied vodka, add peppermint candies to a pint jar and top with vodka. Place the lid on the jar and shake gently. Cover and let sit for a minimum of 4 hours or overnight.
Strain the peppermint vodka infusion into an airtight container. Discard any undissolved peppermints.
To prepare the garnish, place a few peppermint candies inside a plastic bag. Crush with a rolling pin into fine pieces.
Rim the cocktail glass with marshmallow fluff and dip in crushed peppermint.
Add ice to the rimmed glass, then pour in peppermint vodka and coffee liqueur.
Using the back of a spoon, slowly pour heavy cream on top to suspend the cream on top of the alcohol.
Garnish the top with extra crushed peppermint candies. Enjoy!

Ingredients: 1/2 luid ounce agave syrup or simple syrup
1 wedge plus 1 slice lemon or lime, divided,
chili lime seasoning, such as Tajin
Direction: Add vodka, blueberry lemonade, agave syrup, and lime juice to a cocktail shaker.
Fill the cocktail shaker with ice and shake until the outside is frosted, about 30 seconds.
Sprinkle Tajin seasoning on a plate, rub the rim of your favorite glass with a lemon or lime wedge, and dip the glass in seasoning to coat the rim. Strain the cocktail into the glass.
Fill a mixing glass half-full with ice. Add gin, applejack, Lillet Blanc, and orange bitters. Stir until well chilled. Strain into a cocktail glass; top with apple slice.
Gather all ingredients.
Fill a cocktail shaker with ice, and add vodka, banana liqueur, espresso, banana simple syrup, and bitters.
Shake until very cold and frothy, about 30 seconds. Strain into a chilled martini glass.
Grate nutmeg over martini and garnish with espresso beans, banana chips, or skewered banana bread cubes. Serve immediately.
Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

Ingredients: 1 ( 750 ml) bottle gin, such as Broker's London Dry
3 ounces dry Vermouth, such as Dolin's
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Pour 1 cup gin out of the 750 mLbottle. Set aside for another use. Add Vermouth, filtered water, and pepperoncini brine to the gin bottle.
Chill in the freezer for at least 4 hours, or until ready to serve. If desired, serve with a lemon twist garnish.
Gather all ingredients.
Pour out 1 ¼ cups of the vodka bottle. Reserve poured-out vodka for another use.

Pour 1/2 of the remaining vodka from the bottle into a small saucepan and warm over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes (do not boil). Remove from heat and immediately whisk in the espresso powder until fully dissolved and no lumps remain. Allow the mixture to cool for 5-10 minutes before proceeding.
Add the cooled vodka espresso mixture, coffee liquor, simple syrup, and a pinch of sea salt to the vodka bottle. Cap and shake gently to mix.
Freeze for at least 4 hours before serving. Note: mixture will not fully freeze due to the alcohol content.

To serve, fill  a cocktail shaker with ice and add 3 ounces of the mixture. Dilute with ½ ounce water per individual serving. Shake vigorously for 15 to 20 seconds. Strain into a chilled martini or coupe glass. Garnish with 3 coffee beans or a dusting of espresso powder, if desired.
Add ice cubes, gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.

Fill a rocks glass with crushed ice. Strain cocktail into glass, then gently pour crème de mûre over the top to create a layered effect. The crème de mûre will sink down to the bottom of the glass. Garnish with blackberries and a lemon slice.

Ingredients: 2 fresh cherries, pitted, or more to taste, plus more for garnish
Direction: Place cherries and lime juice in a shaker and muddle to loosen the cherry juices.
Fill shaker with ice, add tequila and amaretto, and shake until well blended and slightly frothy.  Strain over ice and garnish with a cherry.

Cocktails.Recipe: 10 Easy Simple Syrup Recipes to Level Up Your Happy Hour

Direction: Fill a cocktail shaker half full with ice. Add coffee, brandy, crème de cacao, half-and-half, and Amaro Averna. Cover and shake until very cold.
Strain into a cocktail glass. Garnish with coffee beans and/ or nutmeg.

Ingredients: 2 tablespoons orange zest, salt, and sugar mix (for sugar rim) (optional, see Note)
2 slices orange or lemon, for garnish
Direction: Gather all your ingredients.
Mix orange zest, sugar, and salt together on a small plate
Rim 2 glasses with lime wedge and rotate in the orange zest mixture.
Combine tequila, orange juice, lime juice, triple sec, and ice cream in a cocktail shaker.
Fill cocktail shaker with ice and shake very well. Strain into the orange-rimmed glasses and garnish with an orange or lemon slice

Ingredients: 2 slices fresh pineapple, plus more for garnish
Direction: Combine pineapple and jalapeno slices in a cocktail shaker and muddle. Pour in tequila, pineapple juice, lime juice, and orange juice. Fill with ice and shake until well combined. Set aside.
Place tajin on a plate.  Rub one side of glass with lime slice and roll in tajin. Strain margarita into the prepared glass and garnish with pineapple slice and jalapeno slice if desired.

Ingredients: 2 fluid ounce lemon and elderflower vodka
Direction: Combine limoncello cream, lemon juice, sweetened condensed milk, heavy cream, and lemon & elderflower vodka in a blender. Add ice; blend on Whip or Frozen Cocktail setting until ice is blended.
Pour into glasses; garnish with vanilla whipped cream, lemon zest, and dried or fresh lemon wheel.
Combine sweet tea, lemonade, and bourbon in a 1-gallon jug. Seal the jug and carefully tilt it upside down a couple time to mix the ingredients.  Refrigerate until ready to serve; serve over ice.
Combine grapefruit juice, gin, Aperol, and simple syrup in a jug and seal tightly. Lightly shake jug to mix. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Lightly shake and serve over ice; garnish with a rosemary sprig.

Combine strawberries, sugar and 3/4 cup water in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook until mixture has thickened slightly and reduced a little, about 10 minutes.
Strain strawberry mixture into a jar and discard solids. Let cool completely and refrigerate until ready to use.

Pour 1 3/4 cups vodka from bottle and reserve for another use. To the remaining vodka, add 1/2 cup cooled strawberry simple syrup, orange liqueur, lime juice, and remaining 1/4 cup water.  Seal the bottle and tilt it gently to mix the ingredients.
Place bottle in freezer for at least 6 hours or until ready to serve.
Lightly shake bottle before serving in a martini glass and garnish individual cosmos with a slice of lime if desired.

Ingredients: ¾ cup Champagne or sparkling wine, chilled
Direction: Gather the ingredients.
Divide orange juice evenly into two flute glasses.
Top with chilled Champagne.
Serve and enjoy!

Ingredients: 1 grapefruit slice or lime slice or both
Direction: Add tequila, lime juice, grapefruit juice, and agave nectar into a cocktail shaker. Add ice and shake until the outside of the shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds.
Pour into a frosted martini glass, leaving enough room for a splash of grapefruit soda. Garnish with a grapefruit slice or lime slice or both.

Ingredients: 1 1/2 cups ice, divided, or as needed
Direction: Sprinkle salt onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with lime wedge and press the moistened rim into the salt; fill the glass with ice.

Fill a cocktail shaker half-full with ice. Add passion fruit juice, tequila, triple sec, and lime juice to the shaker. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds. Strain mixture into the glass and stir. Garnish with lime wedge.
My favorite brand of passion fruit juice is Goya®, which can be found in the international aisle of your grocery store.
Sprinkle salt onto a plate. Moisten the rim of 2 glasses with a lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the salt. Fill glasses with ice. Divide guava nectar between each glass.

Fill a cocktail shaker half-full with ice. Add tequila, triple sec, and lime juice to the shaker. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds. Strain mixture evenly between the glasses and stir. Garnish with remaining lime wedges.
My favorite brand of guava nectar is Jumex®, which can be found in the international aisle of your grocery store.
Pour 1 1/4 cups tequila from the bottle and reserve for another use.
Add lime juice, triple sec, agave, and salt to the bottle of tequila and place top on the bottle. Tilt bottle to lightly shake mixture until agave has been well incorporated.
Place bottle in the freezer for at least 8 hours or until ready to serve.

To serve, add 1 cup ice to a shaker or glass and top with about 1/2 cup of margarita mix.  Shake mixture or pour margarita between two glasses until well blended and slightly frothy. Serve immediately with more ice if desired. This step is important to balance the taste through slight dilution from the ice.
Run a lime wedge around the edge of a glass and rim with salt if desired. Fill cup with ice and add tequila and lime juice Top with cola and add a pinch of salt. Stir and enjoy with a wedge of lime.

Ingredients: 1  tablespoon strawberry preserves, or more to taste
Direction: Add strawberry preserves, tequila, orange liqueur, fresh lime juice, and ice to a jar fitted with a lid or shaker. Close jar and shake until slightly frothy.

For syrup, stir rhubarb, honey, water, and ginger together in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 15 minutes. Remove from heat; let cool completely, about 1 hour.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into an airtight container or jar; discard solids. Syrup can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

For green tea punch, bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Remove from heat and add tea bags. Steep, covered, 5 minutes. Remove tea bags, or strain to remove loose tea. Let tea cool completely, about 1 hour.
Muddle mint in a large pitcher. Add cooled tea, vodka, honey-rhubarb syrup, and lime juice. Chill at least 30 minutes, or up to 12 hours.
Add club soda to a pitcher and stir gently. Serve over ice and garnish with fresh mint and rhubarb stalks.

Ingredients: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger Irish whiskey such as Jameson
1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger Irish cream liqueur
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Combine Irish whiskey and Irish cream liqueur in a glass mug; pour in hot brewed coffee.
Top with whipped cream and a dash of nutmeg.
In a cocktail shaker, combine vodka, passion fruit pulp, simple syrup, lime juice and ice. Shake well until the outside of the shaker is frosted, about 15 seconds.

Strain into a martini glass. Use a Hawthorne cocktail strainer to retain passion fruit seeds in the drink, or use a fine mesh strainer to strain out seeds. Top with chilled Champagne, and garnish with lime wheel.
Add pomegranate juice and elderflower liqueur to a champagne flute. Top with prosecco, pouring gently to preserve the bubbles.
Drop in a few pomegranate arils and garnish with a sprig of rosemary.

Scoop ice into a shaker. Pour in whiskey, peach schnapps, and simple syrup. Squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon. Cover shaker, and shake until the outside of shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds. Pour drink into a glass. Serve.

Ingredients: 1 1/2 luid ounce  Irish cream liqueur, such as Bailey's®
Direction: Pour brown sugar onto a plate. Pour a splash of eggnog on another plate and dip the rim of the glass in eggnog and then in brown sugar.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add eggnog, vodka, and Baileys. Close the shaker and shake until the outside of shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds. Pour into the prepared glass and sprinkle with cinnamon.

Ingredients: 1 1/2 luid ounces orange liqueur, such as Cointreau®
Direction: Pour salt onto a plate. Rub lime wedge around the rim of a glass, and dip the rim of the glass in the salt.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add guava nectar, tequila, Cointreau, lime juice, and agave syrup. Close the shaker and shake until the outside of the shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds. Pour into the salted glass.

In a cocktail shaker, combine lime juice, simple syrup and 6 mint leaves. Use a muddler to crush the leaves for about 10 seconds. Add rum and 1 cup ice. Seal shaker and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain mojito into a glass. Add passion fruit pulp and club soda and gently stir. Fill glass with crushed ice and garnish with remaining mint leaves.

Ingredients: 2  dashes hot sauce, such as Tabasco®
Direction: Place 1/2 teaspoon dry ranch dressing mix on a plate. Run a piece of lime around the rim of glass. Dip rim in dressing mix until coated. Set aside.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add tomato juice, vodka, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco, horseradish and 1/2 teaspoon dry ranch mix. Shake until the outside of the shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds. Pour into the prepared glass.
Fill a mixing glass or cocktail shaker half full with ice. Add bourbon, liqueur, and bitters. Stir or shake until very cold, about 30 seconds.
Strain into 2 glasses. Rub rim of each glass with an orange twist, then garnish each glass with a twist.

Ingredients: 1/2  fluid ounce orange liqueur, such as Cointreau
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Fill a shaker halfway with ice; pour in tequila, orange liqueur, orange juice, lime juice, and marmalade.
Shake until the outside of the shaker is frosted, 15 to 30 seconds.
Pour into a glass; garnish with an orange slice.
Enjoy!
Place celery seed on a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with a lime wedge. Dip rim in celery seed until coated. Set aside.
Fill a shaker with ice. Add carrot juice, vodka, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco, and horseradish. Shake until well combined. Pour into the prepared glass.
Pour chocolate syrup into 2 martini glass; swirl to line the glass, and pour the extra into a cocktail shaker. Place glasses in the freezer until frosted, 5 to 10 minutes.
Add vodka, RumChata, and milk, to the cocktail shaker. Add ice and shake until the outside of the shaker is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds. Strain into coated martini glasses and enjoy.
Sprinkle chili lime seasoning onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with a lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the seasoning. Fill the glass with ice.
Fill a cocktail shaker with tequila, triple sec, lime juice, orange juice, adobo sauce, and agave syrup. Add 1 cup ice. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain margarita into the glass and garnish with remaining lime wedge.
Place Tajin on a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with a lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into Tajin. Set aside.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add tomato juice, tequila, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco, horseradish, and celery seed. Shake until the outside of shaker is frosted; strain into the prepared glass.
Sprinkle celery salt onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the salt. Fill glass with ice.

Add vodka, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco sauce, then fill with Clamato juice and gently stir. Sprinkle in a pinch of celery salt, then garnish with lime wedge, celery stick and other preferred garnishes.

Ingredients: 2 fluid ounces green apple pucker liqueur
1 tablespoon agave syrup or simple syrup
Direction: Add green apple vodka, green apple pucker, lemonade, and agave syrup to a cocktail shaker. Fill the shaker with ice.
Shake very well and pour into 2 frosted martini glasses. Garnish with green apple slices.
Sprinkle salt onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the salt. Fill the glass with ice.

Fill a cocktail shaker with 10 blackberries, reserving 2 blackberries for garnish. Use a muddler to crush berries to release their juices. Add tequila, triple sec, simple syrup and lime juice to the shaker and add 1 cup of ice. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain margarita into the glass and garnish with remaining blackberries.

Ingredients: 1/4 ounce brine from Mezzetta Italian Mix Giardiniera
vegetable pieces from Mezzetta Italian Mix Giardiniera, for garnish
Direction: Combine vodka, tea, and brine in an ice-filled mixing glass; stir well to chill.
Fill a lowball or rocks glass with ice. Strain martini over ice. Garnish with olives and vegetable pieces.
Place sugar, lime juice, blackberries and mint leaves in an old fashioned glass, and mash well with a cocktail muddler. Add soda water and rum; stir. Fill with ice.
Pour Tajin onto a plate. Rub a lime wedge around the rim of a glass, and dip the rim of the glass in Tajin.

Place 3 jalapeno slices into a cocktail shaker and mash well with a cocktail muddler. Add ice to the shaker. Pour in tequila, lime juice, orange juice, and agave syrup; cover and shake until the outside of the shaker has frosted, about 30 seconds. Strain into a chilled glass and garnish with remaining jalapeno slices. Serve immediately.
Spread sugar on a small plate. Rub rims of 2 cocktail glasses with lemon wedge. Dip rims in sugar to coat.

Fill a cocktail shaker half full with ice. Add whiskey, lemon juice, orange liqueur, and raspberry liqueur. Cover and shake until outside of shaker is frosted, about 60 seconds. Strain into prepared glasses. Top each cocktail with 1 1/2 ounces sparkling water and garnish with a raspberry.

Cocktails.Recipe: Big Batch Freezer Lemon Drop Martinis
Direction: Pour vodka, lemon juice, orange liqueur, and simple syrup into a freezer-safe 750ml bottle. Cover tightly, and tilt gently a few times to incorporate ingredients.  Place bottle in the freezer for several hours until very well chilled.
Shake gently before serving. Serve as desired, as in a sugar-rimmed glass.  Store any extra in the freezer until ready to use.
Gather all ingredients.
Stir brewed espresso and simple syrup together in a small pitcher. Pour mixture into ice cube trays and freeze for 8 hours or overnight.
Pour vodka, Kahlúa, and Frangelico into a blender. Add in the espresso ice cubes, and blend until smooth.
Pour frozen mixture into 4 martini glasses. Lightly dust the martini with black onyx cocoa powder. Enjoy!

Cocktails.Recipe: This Matcha Martini Will Be Your Go-to Drink of the Summer
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
In a cocktail shaker filled about 3/4 with ice, add prepared matcha, vodka, creme de cacao, and simple syrup.
Top with the lid, and shake for 1 to 2 minutes, or until frothy.
Strain into a cocktail glass and garnish with more matcha powder, if desired.

Cocktails.Recipe: 20 Fourth of July Cocktails That Are Worthy of Celebration

Direction: Rinse limes and cut the ends off.  Cut each lime in 8 wedges and add to a blender.  Add water, coconut rum, and sweetened condensed milk; blend until creamy.
Fill 3 glasses with ice and strain lemonade over.
Mix salt and coriander together on a small plate. Wipe rim of a margarita glass with lime wedge. Dip rim in salt mixture to coat. Fill glass with crushed ice.

Fill a cocktail shaker half full with ice. Add tequila, celery cordial, lime juice, and bitters to shaker; cover and shake until outside of shaker is frosted, about 60 seconds. Strain into prepared glass and garnish with celery stalk.
Bring water, the 3/4 cup mint, and sugar to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat and add tea bags. Steep for 1 hour.
Strain mixture into a pitcher and add bourbon. Stir until combined.
Muddle 4 mint leaves in a glass. Fill halfway with ice, add a lemon slice, and fill with more ice. Add tea bourbon mixture; garnish with a mint sprig and a lemon wedge.

Ingredients: 2 fluid ounces sweet and sour mix
Direction: Pour 1/4 to 1/2 inch of sugar onto a small, shallow plate. Moisten rim of a rocks glass with a wedge of lime, dip the moistened glass into sugar; set aside.
Scoop ice into a shaker. Pour in strawberry schnapps, vanilla vodka, and sweet and sour mix;  cover and shake until the outside is frosted. Strain into a chilled glass.
Fill a collins glass with ice and set aside.

In a cocktail shaker, combine lime juice, simple syrup and Thai basil leaves. Use a muddler to crush the leaves for about 10 seconds. Add rum and 1 cup of ice. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain mojito into the glass and top with club soda; gently stir. Garnish with lime wedge and Thai basil sprig, if desired.

Ingredients: 6 ice cubes, or more if desired
Direction: Place orange slice and 2 cherries in a rocks glass, and crush with a muddler. Add ice cubes to glass. Add tequila, Cointreau and bitters; stir. Garnish with additional 2 cherries and an orange twist.
Sprinkle salt onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the salt. Fill the glass with ice.

Fill a cocktail shaker with jalapeno slices and strawberries, reserving 1 slice of strawberry for garnish. Use a muddler to crush the jalapeno and strawberries to release their juices. Add tequila, triple sec, lime juice and simple syrup to the shaker and add 1 cup of ice. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain margarita into the glass and garnish with remaining strawberry slice, if desired.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add tequila, lime juice, orange juice, cream of coconut, and coconut milk. Shake until tequila mixture is completely chilled and cream of coconut is incorporated, about 30 seconds. Pour into glass. Serve immediately.

Ingredients: 3  jalapeno slices, or more to taste
3/4 fluid ounces triple sec or other orange liqueur
Direction: Sprinkle chili lime seasoning onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the seasoning. Fill the glass with ice.

Fill a cocktail shaker with tequila and 2 jalapeno slices. Use a muddler to crush the peppers. Add mango nectar, triple sec, and lime juice to the shaker and add 1 cup of ice. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain margarita into the glass and garnish with remaining jalapeno slice, if desired.

Ingredients: 3 jalapeno slices, or more to taste
Direction: Sprinkle chili lime seasoning onto a plate. Moisten the rim of a glass with lime wedge. Press the moistened rim into the seasoning. Fill the glass with ice.

Fill a cocktail shaker with tequila and 2 jalapeno slices. Use a muddler to crush the peppers. Add pineapple juice, triple sec, and lime juice to the shaker and add 1 cup of ice. Seal and shake vigorously until outside is frosted, 10 to 15 seconds.
Strain margarita into the glass and garnish with remaining jalapeno slice, if desired.

Ingredients: 1 teaspoon agave syrup, or to taste
Direction: Pour salt onto a plate. Rub a lime wedge around the rim of a glass, and dip the rim of the glass in the salt.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add tequila, lime juice, orange juice, and agave syrup. Close the shaker and shake until completely chilled, about 30 seconds. Pour into the salted glass. Serve immediately.
Fill a cocktail shaker half full with ice. Add gin, egg white, lemon juice, simple syrup, crème de violette, and bitters. Cover and shake until outside of shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds.
Strain into a measuring cup; discard ice. Return cocktail to shaker; cover and shake until pressure builds and mixture starts to emulsify, about 45 seconds.
Pour club soda into a glass. Slowly strain cocktail into glass, allowing foam to rise. Garnish with lemon wheel.
In a champagne flute, combine pomegranate juice and orange liqueur. Top with champagne and serve.

Ingredients: 3 fluid ounces cranberry vodka (such as Deep Eddy)
Direction: Combine cranberry vodka and lime vodka in a tall glass. Add ice, top off with Sprite, and stir. Garnish with lime slice.

Ingredients: 1  teaspoon  vanilla icing, or as needed
Direction: Rim martini glass with icing and sprinkles; set aside.
Fill a cocktail shaker with ice; pour in rum cream, vodka, and amaretto. Cover and shake until the outside of shaker has frosted. Strain into a chilled glass.

You will need 8 mugs or glass coffee cups. Pour 1 ounce of coffee liqueur into each mug, then add one ounce of brandy and 1/2 ounce of creme de cacao to each serving. Fill each mug with hot coffee, garnish with a dollop of whipped cream, and top with chocolate sprinkles; serve.

Ingredients: 2 fluid ounces freshly squeezed grapefruit juice
1 ½ fluid ounces freshly squeezed pomegranate juice
½ fluid ounce sweet French vermouth
½ ounce cream of balsamic (balsamic glaze)
¼ fluid ounce cold-pressed cranberry juice
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground pink peppercorns
Direction: Place vodka, grapefruit juice, pomegranate juice, vermouth, cream of balsamic, cranberry juice, and peppercorns in a cocktail shaker. Fill shaker with ice and shake well; strain into a martini glass. Sprinkle with orange zest.

Ingredients: 3/4 cup brown sugar substitute, such as Swerve
1/4 cup maple-flavored syrup, such as Pyure®
3 tablespoons homemade  banana syrup, or to taste
1 tablespoon sugar-free  sugar-free  maple flavored syrup, such as Pyure®
Direction: Gather all ingredients.

Combine bananas, brown sugar substitute, and maple syrup substitute in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir until sugar has melted. Add water, increase heat, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in salt, cinnamon, banana extract, maple extract, and vanilla extract. Use an immersion blender to whip until well combined.
For the banana cream foam, combine cream and banana syrup in a glass and use a frother to beat until foamy.

For caramelized bananas, melt butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Stir in maple-flavored syrup. Arrange banana slices in a single layer in the skillet and cook until golden brown and caramelized, 3 to 5 minutes.
Pour coffee into a mug. Combine banana syrup, banana extract and hot milk in a cup and pour over coffee. Top with banana cream foam and caramelized bananas.
Gather all ingredients.
Fill a cocktail shaker with ice, and add vodka, banana liqueur, espresso, banana simple syrup, and bitters.
Shake until very cold and frothy, about 30 seconds. Strain into a chilled martini glass.
Grate nutmeg over martini and garnish with espresso beans, banana chips, or skewered banana bread cubes. Serve immediately.
Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

Coffee Drinks.Recipe: The 4-Ingredient Apple Pie Cold Foam We're Making All Fall
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Place all ingredients in a small measuring cup or jar. Using a handheld milk frother, froth until thick, creamy, and increased to 1/2 cup in volume, about 1 minute.
Pour cold brew into a glass filled with ice and top with desired amount of cold foam.
Garnish with additional apple pie spice. Serve immediately.
Recipe developed by Isabelle Easter

Coffee Drinks.Recipe: 8 Coffee Creamer Recipes That Are So Good, You'll Ditch the Store-Bought Stuff

Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Make espresso. Stir in sugar until dissolved; set aside.
Froth milk with a handheld milk frother in a cup until foamy and doubled in volume, about 60 seconds.
Fill a serving glass with ice cubes. Pour over the espresso, then top with the foamed milk. Serve and enjoy with a straw.

Heat heavy cream and sugar together in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally until sugar dissolves. Whisk in cocoa powder, espresso, vanilla, almond extract and salt. Remove from heat and cool slightly. Stir in half-and-half and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Fill a cocktail shaker half full with ice. Add coffee, brandy, crème de cacao, half-and-half, and Amaro Averna. Cover and shake until very cold.
Strain into a cocktail glass. Garnish with coffee beans and/ or nutmeg.
Preheat the oven’s broiler and set a rack about 6 inches below the heat source. Line a baking sheet with parchment, and place marshmallows on the baking sheet.
Broil until marshmallow tops are well browned, 1 to 2 minutes.

Add water and sugar to a saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring often, until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat; stir in marshmallows, salt, and vanilla and cook, stirring constantly, until creamy.
Strain mixture through a fine sieve and stir in heavy cream. Serve immediately, stirred into coffee.
Gather all ingredients.
Pour espresso and sugar into a cocktail shaker. Add 4 ice cubes, cover, and shake until coffee is frothy and cold and ice has melted.
Fill a glass with ice and pour shaken coffee over ice.
Combine 2 cups water and tea bags in a saucepan; bring to a boil over high heat. Turn off heat and allow tea to steep 10 minutes.

Remove tea bags from the pan and stir in brown sugar, white sugar, molasses, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves. Return pan to high heat and bring to a boil. Simmer until reduced and thickened. Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.
Meanwhile, pour oats into a heat resistant bowl. Bring 2 cups water to a boil and pour over the oats to cover. Let stand 10 minutes.  Drain oats and rinse with cold water.
Combine oats, coconut oil, 1 1/2 cups cold water, and dates in a blender. Blend until smooth and creamy. Pour mixture through a fine sieve and discard solids.
Stir 1/2 cup (or more if desired) of cooled chai mixture into oat milk mixture and refrigerate until ready to use.
Whisk or blend half-and-half, condensed milk, vanilla extract, almond extract, and salt together until well incorporated and smooth.  Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Place coffee, sugar, and water, in that order, in a tall glass. Using a hand-held milk frother, froth mixture until light and fluffy, 1 to 3 minutes.
Add ice cubes to the glass, then pour milk over top.
Whisk or blend half-and-half, condensed milk, peppermint extract, vanilla extract, and cocoa powder together until well incorporated and smooth.  Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Coffee Drinks.Recipe: Top Tips for Making a Perfect Cappuccino at Home Every Time
Ingredients: 1 pinch  ground cinnamon nutmeg, for sprinkling
Direction: Gather the ingredients.
Fill espresso machine reservoir with water.
Spoon ground espresso into portafilter.
“Tamp” or press coffee grounds down using a tamper. Do this 2 to 3 times to make sure grounds are packed tightly.
Place portafilter into your espresso machine's group head, and lock it in place.
Place your drinking vessel under the portafilter, and pull the shot for 23 to 30 seconds (you should have 2 ounces of espresso for a double shot).

Pour milk into either a glass measuring cup or a small metal pitcher. Insert steam wand into container with milk, just under the surface of the milk. Keeping the wand toward the side of the container, move the container up and down so that the wand can incorporate air into the milk. Steam milk until doubled in volume and very foamy, about 20 seconds. Swirl frothed milk a couple of times to incorporate foam into milk.

Immediately top espresso with foamed milk, and sprinkle with cinnamon. When initially poured, cappuccino is only espresso and foam, but the liquid milk quickly settles out of the foam to create the roughly equal parts foam, steamed milk, and espresso.
Gather the ingredients.
Unscrew top and bottom pieces of device. Remove filter basket from bottom half, and pour water into the reservoir.

Replace filter basket in the bottom half, and fill with espresso grounds. Smooth out the grounds, but DO NOT tamp or press down. Wipe away any loose grounds around the edge. Screw top half of the device back onto bottom half.

Set device over medium-low heat with the lid closed. (Make sure the flame is not larger than the device and the device is slightly off-center of the heating element to prevent the handle from getting hot.) On a gas stove, allow the espresso to percolate until the top pot is half full; then turn off the heat, and allow the coffee to finish brewing. Alternatively, on an electric stove, once you hear the coffee percolating, remove from heat, and the residual heat will continue to brew the coffee.

Pour milk into a microwave-safe measuring cup. Microwave on HIGH for 1 minute or until milk is 150 degrees F (65 degrees C). (Alternatively, heat milk in a small saucepan over medium until hot to the touch but not simmering, about 2 minutes.) Use a milk frother, French press, or whisk to froth the milk until very foamy.  Swirl frothed milk a couple of times to incorporate foam into milk.

Immediately top espresso with foamed milk, and sprinkle with cinnamon. When initially poured, cappuccino is only espresso and foam, but the liquid milk quickly settles out of the foam to create the roughly equal parts foam, steamed milk, and espresso.
Recipe developed by Julia Levy
Swirl pistachio cream into a glass. Using a straw, push cream down and around. Add milk. Fill glass to within 1 inch of rim with ice. Pour in espresso.
Gather all ingredients.
Stir together coffee grounds, sugar, cinnamon stick, and vanilla bean paste in an 8- to 12-ounce canning jar. Let stand, covered, at room temperature 8 hours.
Stir in boiling water. Set a sieve over a small bowl; add a coffee filter to sieve. Pour coffee mixture over filter; let stand until liquid has passed through. Discard solids.
Pour liquid into a pint-size sealable bottle or canning jar with a lid and add rum; shake to combine. Chill, covered. Shake before serving. Sip as a liqueur or use in cocktails.
Gather all ingredients.
Stir brewed espresso and simple syrup together in a small pitcher. Pour mixture into ice cube trays and freeze for 8 hours or overnight.
Pour vodka, Kahlúa, and Frangelico into a blender. Add in the espresso ice cubes, and blend until smooth.
Pour frozen mixture into 4 martini glasses. Lightly dust the martini with black onyx cocoa powder. Enjoy!
Fill a 16 ounce glass with ice. Add milk. Add cardamom to espresso and stir to combine. Pour into glass. Top with sweetened condensed milk.
Place water, piloncillo, and cinnamon in a pot. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 8 minutes.
Remove from heat, add coffee, and stir well. Cover pot and steep for 5 minutes. Pour through a fine mesh strainer twice or until free of any coffee granules.
Place oat milk and honey in a tall, microwave-safe cup and heat until hot, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir until well combined. Froth hot oat milk mixture with an immersion blender or with a frothing wand.
Pour coffee into a cup. Using the back of a spoon pour frothed milk over coffee. Pour foam over frothed milk. Sprinkle with cinnamon.

Ingredients: 1 teaspoon brown sugar, or to taste
Direction: Add cookie butter to hot coffee and whisk until cookie butter has dissolved. Stir in brown sugar and vanilla. Pour into a coffee mug.
Froth hot milk with an immersion blender or with a frothing wand. Using the back of a spoon, pour frothed milk over coffee. Pour foam over frothed milk.
Gather all ingredients.
Combine warm water, instant coffee, and sugar in a sealable jar. Seal and shake until foamy.
Pour into a glass full of ice; add milk. Adjust to taste if necessary.
Gather all ingredients.
Pour milk and eggnog into a steaming pitcher and heat to between 145 degrees F to 165 degrees F (65 to 70 degrees C) using the steaming wand.
Brew a shot of espresso; pour into a mug. Pour steamed milk and eggnog into the mug, using a spoon to hold back the foam.
Spoon foam over the top. Sprinkle nutmeg on top of foam.

Ingredients: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger Irish whiskey such as Jameson
1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger Irish cream liqueur
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Combine Irish whiskey and Irish cream liqueur in a glass mug; pour in hot brewed coffee.
Top with whipped cream and a dash of nutmeg.
In a small bowl, mix together the molasses, brown sugar, baking soda, ginger and cinnamon until well blended. Cover and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes.

Add about a 1/4 cup of coffee to each cup, then stir in about a tablespoon of the spice mixture until dissolved. Fill cup to within an inch of the top with coffee. Stir in half and half to taste, then garnish with whipped cream and a light dusting of cloves.

Ingredients: 1 ½ teaspoons vanilla simple syrup (see above) or purchased vanilla syrup (Optional)
2 cups cold brew coffee or iced coffee
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Combine milk and simple syrup in a small measuring cup.
Submerge the end of a milk frother in the mixture.
Froth until consistently foamy, 15 to 20 seconds for skim milk or 2 to 3 minutes for almond milk.
Divide cold brew coffee between 2 glass mugs.
Spoon cold foam over coffee. Sprinkle with nutmeg or cinnamon.
Add heavy whipping cream, milk, chocolate syrup, cocoa powder and vanilla into a tall glass. Whip with a milk frother until until desired consistency is reached.
Serve over cold brew coffee.

Break 4 ounces of the white chocolate into small pieces and place in a medium microwave-safe bowl; microwave on HIGH, stirring at 30-second intervals, until melted, about 1 1/2 minutes. Spoon about 1 tablespoon of the melted chocolate into each of 6 (1 3/4-inch) silicone ball molds. Immediately flip mold over onto a cutting board or plate to allow chocolate to drip off and coat the mold. Let stand 2 minutes. Flip back over and use an offset spatula to scrape the tops of molds to clean them off, placing any dripped chocolate back into the bowl. Place silicone mold in freezer to set, about 5 minutes. Release chocolate "cups" from silicone molds; set aside. Repeat with another 4 ounces of chocolate.
While the molds chill, stir together beverage mix and pumpkin pie spice in a small bowl. Spoon 2 teaspoons of the mixture into 6 of the "cups."

Place the bowl of the leftover melted chocolate back in the microwave; microwave on HIGH until melted, about 30 seconds. Spoon or pour into a small zip-top plastic bag or piping bag and snip off 1/16-inch of the corner. Pipe a thin chocolate line along the edge of the 6 filled white chocolate cups. Place remaining 6 cups on top, using the white chocolate line as glue. Smooth out with your finger, and gently place in silicone mold; freeze until set, about 5 minutes.
Remove the balls from freezer, and dip an offset spatula in very hot water; use it to smooth out edges of the chocolate ball seam. Set aside.

Break remaining 2 ounces of chocolate into pieces, and place in a small microwave-safe bowl; microwave on HIGH until melted, about 30 seconds. Add food coloring, and stir to combine. Place in a separate ziplock bag and snip off 1/16-inch from a corner. Pipe in a zig-zag pattern on the balls. Freeze until set, about 5 minutes.
To serve, brew an 8- to 10-ounce cup of your favorite coffee. Place a bomb in the hot cup of coffee and stir to melt.

Ingredients: 1 cup strongly brewed black coffee, cooled
Direction: Gather the ingredients.
Blend ice, coffee, milk, caramel sauce, and sugar together in a blender on high speed until smooth.
Pour into two 16-ounce glasses.
Combine ice, coffee, Almond Breeze Original Almondmilk, Almond Breeze Vanilla Almondmilk Creamer, chocolate syrup and chocolate chips in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Serve in glasses.
Combine powdered sugar, cocoa powder, cinnamon, and chili powder in the bottom of a mug.
Pour hot coffee on top and stir until dissolved. Pour in half-and-half creamer and stir.
Top with whipped cream and sprinkle with cinnamon, if desired.
Use flavored creamer to change it up depending on the season.
Whisk boiling water, instant coffee, and sugar together until coffee is dissolved. Continue to whisk until mixture becomes thick and forms a peak, 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour milk into a glass. Pour the frothy coffee on top of the milk.

Coffee Drinks.Recipe: How to Make a Cafe Latte
Ingredients: 1 ⅓ cups hot freshly brewed dark roast espresso coffee
Direction: Gather the ingredients.
Heat milk in a saucepan set over medium-low heat. Whisk briskly with a wire whisk to create foam.
Brew espresso and pour into four cups. Pour in milk, holding back the foam with a spoon. Spoon foam over the top.

Ingredients: 4 ounces Gevalia® Cold Brew Concentrate - House Blend
Direction: Pour vanilla syrup into a drinking glass.
Add ice cubes, then pour in milk.
Slowly pour in cold brew concentrate.
Drizzle drink with caramel sauce.
This recipe was developed by this Allrecipes Allstar as part of a campaign sponsored by Gevalia.
Gather all ingredients.
Combine sweetened condensed milk, skim milk, and vanilla in an airtight container; shake well to blend. Label the container with the expiration date of the milk used.

Ingredients: 1 fluid ounce coffee-flavored liqueur (such as Kahlua®)
Direction: Stir together coffee liqueur and tequila in a mug. Pour in hot coffee and top with whipped cream.
Gather all ingredients.
Pour Baileys into a cocktail shaker.
Pour vodka into the cocktail shaker.
Pour espresso into the cocktail shaker.
Add ice into the cocktail shaker; shake well.
Strain into a martini glass. Enjoy!
Gather all ingredients.
Combine milk and brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat. Heat until frothy and close to simmering, about 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low; whisk in caramel sauce and vanilla.
Stir in coffee.

Ingredients: 2 cups filtered water, at room temperature
Direction: Pour ground coffee into a French press container and add water. Place plunger lid on top and press the plunger down 1 to 2 inches to make sure all coffee grounds are fully submerged; do not press all the way down. Let coffee steep at room temperature for 16 to 18 hours.
Strain coffee through a coffee filter in a small strainer. Transfer to an airtight bottle or jar and keep in the refrigerator for up to a week.
Fill a glass with ice and add equal parts of cold brew and water or milk.
Pour milk into a steaming pitcher and heat to 145 to 165 degrees F (65 to 70 degrees C) using the steaming wand of an espresso machine.
Pour espresso over vanilla syrup in a large coffee mug. Pour steamed milk over espresso, using a spoon to hold back the foam. Spoon foam over top.

Ingredients: 2 teaspoons half-and-half cream, or to taste
1 teaspoon white sugar, or to taste
Direction: Mix ground coffee, allspice, and cinnamon together in a small bowl; add to the filter of a drip coffee maker. Pour 4 cups water into the coffee maker and turn on machine. Pour into 2 cups when coffee finishes dripping; stir in cream and sugar.

You will need 8 mugs or glass coffee cups. Pour 1 ounce of coffee liqueur into each mug, then add one ounce of brandy and 1/2 ounce of creme de cacao to each serving. Fill each mug with hot coffee, garnish with a dollop of whipped cream, and top with chocolate sprinkles; serve.
Bring sugar and water to a boil in a 3-quart saucepan over medium heat. Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in instant coffee, and allow to cool, 30 to 45 minutes.
When cool, stir in vodka and vanilla extract. Pour into clean bottles. Close the bottles tightly and store in a cool dark place.

Ingredients: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger Irish cream liqueur
Direction: Pour hot brewed coffee into a glass mug. Stir in Irish cream liqueur.

Ingredients: ¾ fluid ounce triple sec (such as Bols®)
2 ½ fluid ounces coffee-flavored liqueur (such as Kahlua®)
Direction: Pour sugar into a shallow dish. Wet the rim of a wine glass or Irish coffee mug and dip in sugar to coat. Add rum and triple sec. Use a long match or lighter to carefully ignite the mixture. Turn glass slowly until sugar begins to caramelize. Pour in coffee liqueur to put out the flame. Top with hot coffee.

Coffee Drinks.Recipe: 37 Coffee Shop Drinks and Treats You Can Make at Home

Ingredients: 2 teaspoons white sugar, or to taste
Direction: Combine instant coffee, milk, vanilla, sugar, ice cubes, and chocolate syrup in a blender; blend until smooth.

Ingredients: ½ cup Gevalia® Cold Brew Concentrate - Vanilla
2 teaspoons white sugar, or to taste
1 tablespoon whipped topping (such as Cool Whip®)
2 teaspoons caramel ice cream topping, or to taste
Direction: Place cold brew concentrate, milk, 2 tablespoons caramel ice cream syrup, and sugar in blender; blend until mixed, 5 to 10 seconds. Add ice cubes and blend well, about 5 seconds. Pour into a glass.
Serve topped with whipped topping and a drizzle of caramel syrup.
This recipe was developed by this Allrecipes Allstar as part of a campaign sponsored by Gevalia.

Whisk 4 ounces cream, maple syrup, pumpkin purée, pumpkin pie spice, and vanilla extract together in a microwave-safe bowl. Heat pumpkin mixture in the microwave in 30-second intervals, stirring between intervals, until heated through and completely blended, 1 to 3 minutes.
Pour remaining 10 ounces cream, pumpkin mixture, and sweetened condensed milk into a container; cover with a lid, and shake until completely mixed. Store in the refrigerator.

Pour milk into a steaming pitcher and heat to 145 degrees F to 165 degrees F (65 to 70 degrees C) using the steaming wand. Measure the white chocolate syrup into a large coffee mug. Brew espresso, then add to mug. Pour the steamed milk into the mug, using a spoon to hold back the foam. Top with whipped cream and serve.

Pour milk into a steaming pitcher and heat to 145 degrees F to 165 degrees F (65 to 70 degrees C) using the steaming wand. Measure the chocolate syrup into a large coffee mug. Brew espresso, then add to mug. Pour the steamed milk into the mug, using a spoon to hold back the foam. Top with whipped cream.

Ingredients: 1 cup boiling water, or as needed
Direction: Place butter, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and vanilla extract in the bottom of an Irish coffee glass. Pour in rum and hot water. Stir.

Ingredients: 2 teaspoons white sugar, or to taste
1 tablespoon whipped cream topping, or to taste (Optional)
Direction: Mix half-and-half, sugar, and pumpkin pie spice together in a coffee mug. Pour coffee into mug; stir to blend.
Heat in microwave until hot, about 15 seconds. Top with whipped cream.

Ingredients: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger freshly brewed espresso
Direction: Pour milk into a steaming pitcher and heat to 145 to 165 degrees F (65 to 70 degrees C) using the steaming wand. Pour flavored syrup into a large coffee mug. Add espresso, then pour in steamed milk, using a spoon to hold back the foam. Spoon foam over the top.
Pour the coffee into a mug. Stir in the coffee liqueur and tequila. Garnish with whipped topping, cinnamon, and cocoa powder.
Combine half-and-half, sweetened condensed milk, and vanilla extract together in a container with a lid; cover container and shake vigorously until creamer is smooth.

Ingredients: ¼ cup freshly squeezed lemon juice
1 teaspoon stevia powder, or to taste
Direction: Combine coffee, ice cubes, lemon juice, and stevia in a glass. Stir. Garnish with a slice of lemon.
Combine milk, banana, and simple syrup in a blender; blend until very smooth, about 1 minute.
Fill two 16-ounce glasses with ice cubes. Divide coffee between the glasses. Pour banana milk on top, dividing it evenly between the glasses.
Place coffee and cardamom in the filter of your coffee machine. Place enough water to make 2 cups of coffee in the machine. Turn on the coffee machine.
Pour brewed coffee into 2 coffee cups, and stir 1 tablespoon sweetened condensed milk into each cup. Serve.

Ingredients: 2 tablespoons sugar-free chocolate syrup, or more to taste
Direction: Heat 1/4 cup coffee in microwave in a mug until warmed, about 30 seconds. Stir cocoa mix into the coffee until dissolved.
Fill a large glass with ice cubes. Pour 1 cup cold coffee and almond milk over the ice cubes; stir the cocoa mixture and chocolate syrup into the coffee and almond milk.

Ingredients: 1 teaspoon cocoa powder, or more to taste
½ teaspoon vanilla extract, or more to taste
Direction: Blend milk, ice cubes, sugar, instant coffee granules, cocoa powder, and vanilla extract in a blender until smooth.
Lightly coat the inside of a glass with chocolate syrup. Pour the coffee mixture into the glass. Top with whipped cream to serve.
Heat milk and brown sugar in a small saucepan until frothy, close to simmering. Reduce heat to low. Whisk in cookie butter and cinnamon, then mix in coffee.

Ingredients: ½ pound coarsely ground coffee beans
Direction: Put coffee grounds in a large container. Slowly pour water over grounds.
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and steep at room temperature for 18 to 24 hours.

Line a strainer with several layers of cheesecloth and place atop a pitcher; strain coffee through the cheesecloth into the pitcher. Discard the grounds. To get a clearer brew, strain coffee again through coffee filters. Store in refrigerator.

Ingredients: 3 tablespoons chocolate syrup, or more to taste
Direction: Stir espresso and sweetened condensed milk together in a bowl. Add milk and stir; pour into a blender. Add ice and chocolate syrup to the espresso mixture. Blend until smooth.

Ingredients: 4 cups ice cubes, or as needed
1 cup white sugar, or to taste
Direction: Add 2 cups ice cubes to a 2-quart pitcher. Slowly pour coffee over ice; stir until ice is melted. Stir in sugar; mix thoroughly until completely dissolved. Add milk, stirring just until combined. Stir in remaining 2 cups ice, adding more as needed; refrigerate until well chilled, about 30 minutes.
Fill a tall glass with ice; stir coffee mixture, then pour into glass. Or pour into sterilized serving-size glass bottles or insulated tumblers.
For the coffee, doubling your normal preferred strength is a good rule of thumb.

You can stir in your favorite chocolate syrup, to taste, for a chocolate mocha coffee drink. You can also replace half the milk with your favorite liquid coffee creamer, such as vanilla, Irish cream, etc., or substitute half-and-half for milk for a very rich coffee drink.

Ingredients: 1 packet granular no-calorie sucralose sweetener (such as Splenda)
Direction: Pour coffee into an ice cube tray; freeze until coffee ice cubes form, 1 to 2 hours.
Combine coffee ice cubes, soy milk, chocolate syrup, peanut butter, vanilla extract, and no-calorie sweetener in a blender. Cover and blend until frothy.

Ingredients: ginger ale or lemon lime soda, such as Sprite
Direction: Fill a cocktail shaker with ice; add rum, coconut pineapple juice, lime juice, and agave syrup. Shake until the outside of shaker is frosted, about 30 seconds.
Pour into a glass filled with ice, and top off with ginger ale. Garnish with lime and pineapple.

For syrup, stir rhubarb, honey, water, and ginger together in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for 15 minutes. Remove from heat; let cool completely, about 1 hour.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into an airtight container or jar; discard solids. Syrup can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

For green tea punch, bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Remove from heat and add tea bags. Steep, covered, 5 minutes. Remove tea bags, or strain to remove loose tea. Let tea cool completely, about 1 hour.
Muddle mint in a large pitcher. Add cooled tea, vodka, honey-rhubarb syrup, and lime juice. Chill at least 30 minutes, or up to 12 hours.
Add club soda to a pitcher and stir gently. Serve over ice and garnish with fresh mint and rhubarb stalks.

To make the salted grapefruit cordial: Remove strips of zest from 1 ruby grapefruit with a vegetable peeler, avoiding any white pith. Stir grapefruit zest and sugar together in a jar. Chill, covered, for 24 hours.

Squeeze juice from the grapefruit and measure out 1/2 cup juice. Pour 1/2 cup grapefruit juice, fresh lime juice, and water over the sugar mixture in the jar. Stir in kosher salt. Stir or shake mixture to dissolve sugar. Strain out zest; chill for 1 hour or cover and keep chilled for up to 3 days.
To make the punch: Combine salted grapefruit cordial, grapefruit juice, and lime juice in a punch bowl. Chill until ready to serve; pour in club soda before serving with citrus ice ring, if using.

To make a citrus ice ring: Fill an ice ring mold with very thin half slices of grapefruit and very thin slices of lime. Fill ring halfway with water; freeze until firm, about 30 minutes. Add more water to fill mold, freeze until firm, about 2 hours.

Ingredients: 8 hibiscus tea bags (or 3 tablespoons dried hibiscus flowers
Direction: Heat  water, orange juice, and pure maple syrup just to a boil in a Dutch oven. Remove from heat. Add 8 tea bags (or dried flowers). Cover and steep for 5 to 7 minutes.
Remove tea bags (or strain). Add mezcal and chile liqueur. Keep warm over very low heat or transfer to a slow cooker set to Keep Warm. Serve in mugs; garnish with orange slices studded with cloves.

Ingredients: 1 cinnamon stick, plus more for serving
1/3 cup maple syrup, plus more for garnish
Direction: Steep tea bag and cinnamon stick in the boiling water 5 minutes or according to package directions. Discard tea bag and cinnamon stick. Let cool.
Combine tea, apple cider, lemon juice, and maple syrup in a pitcher. Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 days.

For garnish, pour maple syrup onto one small plate and Demerara sugar onto another. Dip rims of serving glasses first in maple syrup, then in sugar. Fill glasses with ice and pour punch over. Garnish each with a lemon wedge and cinnamon stick.

Ingredients: 3 fluid ounces cranberry vodka (such as Deep Eddy)
Direction: Combine cranberry vodka and lime vodka in a tall glass. Add ice, top off with Sprite, and stir. Garnish with lime slice.

Ingredients: 1 cinnamon stick, plus more for serving
1 or 2 small oranges, thinly sliced, plus more for serving
Direction: Combine cranberry juice cocktail, granulated sugar, whole cloves, cinnamon stick, and orange slices in a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a boil; stir until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 to 20 minutes.
Allow to cool slightly, and ladle into punch cups. Float one orange slice in each cup and garnish with a cinnamon stick. Serve warm.

Ingredients: 2 quarts lime sherbet, sitting at room temperature for a few minutes to soften
2 cups pineapple juice, plus more for coating glass rims
1 glass sugar, for coating glass rims
Direction: Scoop softened lime sherbet into the bottom of a large punch bowl.
Pour the lemon-lime soda, Hawaiian Punch, and 2 cups pineapple juice over the sherbet and stir.

Place red sanding sugar in a shallow dish, and some additional pineapple juice in a separate shallow dish. Dip the rims of your serving glasses in the pineapple juice, then in the sanding sugar to coat the rims generously.
Ladle the punch into the prepared glasses.

Bring water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Stir in sugar, cinnamon stick, and star anise. Remove from heat and add tea bags. Let steep for 3 minutes (or according to package directions for strongest tea). Remove tea bags. Let cool to room temperature, about 1 hour. Remove and discard cinnamon stick and star anise.
Stir together tea mixture, orange juice, whiskey, and lemon juice in a punch bowl or pitcher. Chill until cold, about 2 hours or up to overnight.
Garnish with tangerine slices and additional star anise. Ladle into ice-filled glasses. Top each with a tangerine slice.
Oolong teas vary widely in flavor and can fall somewhere between green and black teas. A fruity or malty oolong is especially nice in this punch, but you can use any tea you enjoy.
Recipe developed by Marianne Williams

Ingredients: 1 (16 ounce) can frozen pineapple juice concentrate
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
2 (2 liter) bottles lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage, chilled
Direction: In a punch bowl, combine pineapple juice concentrate, orange juice concentrate and vodka. Pour in lemon-lime soda. Float cherries and orange slices on top. Add ice before serving.

Ingredients: ½ cup dark rum (such as Meyer's®)
¼ cup coconut-flavored rum (such as Malibu®)
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Stir pineapple juice, orange juice, 151 proof rum, dark rum, coconut-flavored rum, lime juice, and grenadine syrup together in a punch bowl.
Float orange slices, lime slices, and lemon slices in the punch.
Ladle the punch into ice filled glasses, or chill the punch in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

Punch.Recipe: Budget Jungle Juice for a Crowd
Ingredients: 4 quarts pineapple and orange juice blend
Direction: Gather the ingredients.
Pour orange drink, pink lemonade, pineapple-orange juice blend, vodka, rum, and fruit punch into a large punch bowl or container; stir well.
Serve and enjoy!

Heat port wine in a large stockpot with a lid over medium heat until just below the simmering point. Add bourbon and rum; heat until just below simmering. Save the bottles and their caps for storing leftover glögg.
Meanwhile, place cinnamon stick, orange peel, cloves, and cardamom pods in the center of the cheesecloth square. Gather edges of the cheesecloth and tie with kitchen twine to secure; set aside.

When wine mixture is very hot but not boiling, carefully light it with a long-handled match. Wearing a heatproof cooking mitt, carefully pour sugar into the flames; let mixture burn for 1 minute. Place the lid on the stockpot to extinguish the flames and turn off the heat. Let mixture cool, covered, about 10 minutes.
Add the cheesecloth spice bundle, raisins, and almonds to warm wine mixture; let it cool to room temperature, about 1 hour.
Strain cooled glögg and reserve the raisins and almonds.

To serve: Pour glögg into a saucepan and warm over medium-low heat until hot but not simmering, about 5 minutes. Ladle 3 ounces of warmed glögg into a small coffee cup or a small Swedish-style glögg mug, and garnish each serving with a few reserved raisins and almonds.

Punch.Recipe: 9 Old-School Punch Recipes That Deserve a Comeback

Ingredients: 1 (64 fluid ounce) bottle fruit punch, chilled
1 (64 fluid ounce) bottle unsweetened pineapple juice, chilled
Direction: Combine ginger ale, fruit punch, and pineapple juice together in a punch bowl; add scoops of sherbet into the punch. Wait for the sherbet to begin melting, approximately 10 minutes; stir gently and serve.

Ingredients: 1 (64 fluid ounce) bottle orange juice, chilled
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Combine fruit punch and orange juice in a punch bowl.
Slowly pour ginger ale down the side of the bowl to retain carbonation.
Ready to serve. Enjoy!

Ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Steep tea bags in 2 cups boiling water for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, place remaining 3 cups boiling water in a 9x13-inch pan. Stir in sugar until dissolved. Stir in brandy, lemonade concentrate, and orange juice concentrate until combined.
Remove tea bags and stir tea into brandy mixture.
Freeze 8 hours to overnight.
To serve, scoop desired amount into a glass. Fill the glass with lemon-lime soda; stir.
Gather all ingredients.
Scoop lime sherbet into a punch bowl.
Pour in ginger ale and pineapple juice.
Stir well.
Stir in maraschino cherries and float lemon and lime slices in the punch.

Ingredients: 2 (3 ounce) packages strawberry flavored Jell-O mix
2 (2 liter) bottles lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage
Direction: Bring water, sugar, and strawberry-flavored gelatin to a boil in a large saucepan; boil for 3 minutes. Stir in pineapple juice, lemon juice, and orange juice.
Divide mixture into two separate containers and freeze.
Combine contents of 1 container frozen juice mixture with 1 bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage in a punch bowl; stir until slushy. Repeat with remaining portions as needed.

Ingredients: 4 ¾ cups coffee-flavored liqueur (such as Kahlua®)
1 pinch ground nutmeg, or to taste
Direction: Combine ice cream, milk, rum, coffee liqueur, and vodka in a large punch bowl; whisk until frothy and liquified.
Ladle into punch glasses and garnish with nutmeg.

Ingredients: 1 cup fresh raspberries, blackberries, blueberries, or halved strawberries
Direction: Dissolve sugar in tap water in a large pitcher. Add orange slices, lime slices, and wine. Stir in ice cubes until cold. Top with sparkling water. Serve in red-wine glasses, with fresh berries in each glass.

Ingredients: 1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage
1 (64 fluid ounce) bottle white cranberry juice
1 (0.13 ounce) package blue, berry flavored unsweetened drink mix
1 cup white sugar, or to taste
Direction: Stir lemon-lime soda, white cranberry juice, and drink mix together in a large punch bowl until well mixed. Stir in sugar until desired sweetness is reached.
Float scoops of ice cream on top. The ice cream will start to melt and look like frothy white clouds floating on top.

Ingredients: 4 (12 fluid ounce) cans or bottles lemon-lime soda
½  fresh pineapple - peeled, cored, and cut into chunks
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Stir Moscato wine, lemon-lime soda, brandy, peach schnapps, peaches, strawberries, mangos, pineapple chunks, and raspberries together in a large container.
Chill the sangria for 8 hours or overnight. Serve and enjoy!

Ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
Direction: In a punch bowl, combine orange juice, water and pineapple juice; chill. Stir in ginger ale just before serving.

Ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
Direction: Place sherbet and frozen orange juice concentrate in a punch bowl. Allow to thaw for 10 to 15 minutes. Stir in ginger ale.
Place 9 cups of watermelon cubes in a blender; blend on high until very smooth. Strain juice through a mesh strainer into a large pitcher.

Pour wine, vodka, triple sec, and simple syrup into the pitcher; stir to combine. Add remaining 3 cups of watermelon cubes, orange sections, blueberries, and lime quarters; chill sangria for 4 hours before serving.

Ingredients: 4 (750 milliliter) bottles dry white wine, chilled
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Combine peach schnapps, cognac, sugar, sliced oranges, and sliced mangos in a pitcher; stir and chill for at least an hour.
Pour fruit mixture into a large punch bowl. Stir in chilled white wine and ginger ale.
Ladle into glasses with some of the sliced fruit and serve.

Ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
Direction: Pour pineapple juice and orange juice concentrate into an empty gallon milk jug or pitcher; shake to mix. Pour in lemon-lime soda. You may need to let the fizz settle and then return to pouring. Leave some room at the top of the gallon pitcher to allow for expansion as it freezes. Freeze for 8 to 10 hours.
Let the punch start to thaw 2 to 3 hours before serving. Serve slushy.

Ingredients: 1 (750 milliliter) bottle chilled mild red wine (such as Lambrusco)
Direction: Mix wine, apple, strawberries, raspberries, cherries, blueberries, blackberries, and brandy together in a pitcher; refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Stir lemon-lime soda into wine mixture.

Ingredients: 1 (2 ounce) jar instant coffee granules (such as Nescafe®)
Direction: Stir boiling water, sugar, and instant coffee together in a bowl until dissolved; cool in refrigerator, 30 minutes to overnight.
Pour coffee mixture into a punch bowl; add milk, vanilla ice cream, and chocolate ice cream. Stir until ice cream begins to melt.

Ingredients: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate
1 (46 fluid ounce) can sweetened pineapple juice
Direction: In a 2 gallon punch bowl, combine orange juice concentrate, pineapple juice, lemon juice and sugar. Stir in water.
In a 2 quart pitcher, combine the lemon juice, water and sugar. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Chill in refrigerator.
Spoon the sorbet into the bottom of a punch bowl. Slowly pour the soda over the sorbet. Use the back of a spoon to soften the sorbet until combined. Serve.

Ingredients: 2 (10 ounce) packages frozen strawberries, partially thawed
Direction: In a large punch bowl, combine champagne, ginger ale and strawberries. Gently stir and serve.

Ingredients: ¼ cup brown sugar, plus 1 tablespoon divided
Direction: Combine apple cider, apple brandy, ¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon brown sugar, honey, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, pepper, and salt in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Simmer until flavors combine, about 10 minutes.
Pour apple cider mixture into heat-proof mugs. Twist orange zest strips between fingers to release essential oils; drop 1 into each mug. Add 1 cinnamon stick to each mug.

Ingredients: 2 (10 ounce) packages frozen sliced strawberries, thawed
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed
2 (750 milliliter) bottles chilled rosé wine, such as white Zinfandel
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Stir the strawberries, lemonade concentrate, rosé wine, and pineapple juice in a punch bowl until combined.
Stir in the ginger ale just before serving.
Enjoy!
In a pitcher, combine sugar and tea. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Stir in orange juice, pineapple juice and lemonade. Chill in refrigerator for 4 hours.
Just before serving, pour chilled juice mixture into a punch bowl and stir in ginger ale.

Ingredients: ½ liter lemon-lime soda (such as Sprite®)
Direction: Mix pineapple juice, orange juice, lemonade, and water in a large punch bowl. Stir in ginger ale and lemon-lime soda.

In a slow-cooker or a large pot over low heat, combine apple cider, orange juice and lemon juice. Season with cloves, ginger and nutmeg. Bring to a simmer. If using a slow cooker, allow to simmer all day. Serve hot.

Ingredients: 1 tablespoon white sugar, or more to taste
Direction: Combine red wine, ice cubes, blueberries, raspberries, strawberries, orange-flavored liqueur, orange juice, and sugar in a blender; process until smooth. Serve immediately or freeze.
In a pitcher, combine lime juice, simple syrup, rum and orange juice. Add a few dashes of bitters and some grated nutmeg to taste. Serve chilled over ice.

Ingredients: 1 (6 ounce) can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
1 (6 ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate, thawed
1 (2 liter) bottle lemon-lime flavored carbonated beverage, chilled
Direction: Gather all ingredients.
Place rhubarb in a large saucepan with water to cover. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and cook until tender.
Drain; mash or purée in a blender.
Stir together rhubarb purée, sugar, orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, gin, and water.
Freeze for 1 to 3 hours, depending on the consistency you like.
Place scoops of the frozen mixture into serving glasses and fill the rest of the glass with lemon-lime soda.

Ingredients: 1 (32 fluid ounce) bottle apple juice, chilled
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen cranberry juice concentrate
Direction: In a large punch bowl, combine apple juice, cranberry juice concentrate and orange juice. Stir until dissolved, then slowly pour in the ginger ale.
Thinly slice the apple vertically, forming whole apple slices. Float apple slices on top of punch.

Ingredients: 2 tablespoons white sugar, or to taste
Direction: Grate watermelon with a fork from the rind into a large bowl, leaving no large chunks. Stir water, pineapple, evaporated milk, and coconut into the grated watermelon. Add sugar; stir until dissolved. Squeeze lime juice into the watermelon mixture.
In a pitcher, combine lime juice, water, sugar and honey. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Chill in refrigerator.

Ingredients: 2 (12 fluid ounce) cans frozen orange juice concentrate
1 (12 fluid ounce) can frozen lemonade concentrate
Direction: In a blender, combine bananas, sugar, and 3 cups water. Blend until smooth. Pour into a large bowl and stir in pineapple juice. Blend in orange juice concentrate, lemonade concentrate, and 3 cups water. Divide into 3 plastic containers and freeze until solid, 4 hours to overnight.

Before making this punch, place the orange juice, ginger ale, and Champagne into the refrigerator for several hours to ensure they are well chilled.

Pour wine into glasses, and top off with club soda. Serve immediately.

Strain lemonade into a pitcher. Fill six (6- to 8-ounce) glasses with crushed ice; add lemonade.

Fill a cocktail shaker with ice. Add cranberry juice, vodka, schnapps, and lime juice. Cover and shake until the outside of the shaker has frosted. Strain into a chilled martini glass to serve.
